lead.headline: The tax agency revoked 108 nonprofits for not filing, yet its own e-file index holds a return from those years
lead.number: 108 auto-revoked 2019-2026 with a return received for one of the three missed years; 59 still unreinstated and off the exempt list; 27 quietly put back without a recorded reinstatement
lead.watch_out: A late or wrong-form return received before the revocation date may not legally stop auto-revocation; get the IRS rule in writing. The claimed 6x time trend is an e-file-mandate artifact; drop it.

sources.page_context: White nationalist's nonprofit loses tax-exempt status By Caitlin Yilek Washington Examiner Published March 13, 2017 7:20pm EDT | Updated March 14, 2017 8:13am EDT The IRS has stripped white nationalist Richard Spencer's nonprofit of its tax-exempt status over failure to file tax returns after 2012. Spencer told the Los Angeles Times on Monday that an IRS error was to blame for the National Policy Institute's failure to file federal tax returns. The IRS had reportedly misclassified Spencer's group, but fixed the error in February. On Monday the IRS' updated records said the group's tax-exempt status was stripped retroactively to May 2016.
